channel.title: Counter Notes · the kitchen edit
channel.description: Considered kitchen gear and useful buying questions.

item.title: Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?
item.description: Separate baskets, one larger drawer or French doors: compare the layouts before counting presets.

item.title: A no-hype checklist for comparing air fryer capacity
item.description: Combined quarts are only the starting point. Compare the basket layout and leave unmeasured serving estimates out of it.

item.title: How should you assess cleanup and counter-space trade-offs?
item.description: Measure where it will live, check the removable parts, and separate appliance dimensions from required clearance.

item.title: What should you ask before buying a multi-function kitchen appliance?
item.description: A practical set of questions about layout, modes, exact variants and the tools already in your kitchen.

item.title: How many quarts of air fryer do you actually need?
item.description: Capacity is the one number every buyer looks at and almost nobody can translate. Six quarts of what? Here is the only honest way to answer it: read what each manufacturer says its own basket is sized for, and then do the arithmetic on the dimensions, because the quarts figure is measured by the brand and no two measure it the same way.

item.title: Two baskets or one big one? A trade you cannot undo later
item.description: The dual-basket pitch is not really about capacity. It is about finishing two foods at the same time, which is a timing problem, not a volume problem. Once you see it that way, the comparison gets much easier - and one of these two stops being the sensible default for most kitchens.

item.title: Air fryer or air fryer toaster oven: the door is the decision
item.description: Basket, or oven with doors? Most comparisons answer with a list of extra modes. That is the wrong first question. The mechanical difference is the door: a basket you pull out, or a front that swings open so a sheet pan can slide in. Everything else follows from that, including which of them can roast a chicken.

item.title: Hi-Fry, 450 F and 400 F: why two official pages disagree about one fryer
item.description: On one product, Amazon's title says the Hi-Fry option reaches 450 F. The manufacturer's own page for the same model states a range that stops at 400 F. This is not a typo you can pick a side of. It is a difference between a listing written for a category and a specification written for a machine - and it is exactly the kind of thing a buying decision should be made around, not through.

item.title: Will it fit? The exact footprint of all three, in inches
item.description: Return reasons are usually not performance. They are the cupboard, the splash-back and the height of the cabinet above the counter. So before the capacity debate: here are the three sets of numbers that decide whether the machine is going to live on your counter or in a car park queue at the returns desk.

item.title: 24 presets or 25? A field guide to spec-sheet drift on appliance pages
item.description: The Emeril oven's Amazon title says 24 one-touch preset options. Its own product page says 25 cooking pre-sets in one tile and describes a 10-in-1 oven in the paragraph below. The model number on the store page ends in 02A; the one in the Amazon specification block ends in 02X. This is not a scandal - it is normal, it is everywhere, and once you can see it you cannot shop the same way again.

item.title: Air fryer vs your oven: what three spec sheets can settle, and what they cannot
item.description: 'Air fryer vs oven' is really three questions wearing one coat. The three machines on this site are two basket fryers and a 26 Qt countertop oven with French doors, and they answer it three different ways. Here is what their official pages actually settle - and the one appliance in this comparison nobody on this site has read a line about: yours.

item.title: Are air fryers worth it? What three spec sheets support - and what they never will
item.description: A verdict on 'worth it' is always really a price, a habit and a kitchen. This site can print none of those. What it can do is strip the trend to its checkable parts: what these three machines state on their official pages, which claims the pages themselves contradict, and who each size is actually built for.

item.title: Seven questions to ask before buying a multi-function kitchen appliance
item.description: Retained guide; original date and verification scope apply. Ten modes sounds like ten appliances. Before you clear the counter, here is how to tell which of them you will actually use, and which number on the box to trust.

item.title: Do you need a meat thermometer for an air fryer? What the USDA chart says
item.description: Retained guide; original date and verification scope apply. An air fryer's dial sets the temperature of the air, not of the chicken. The federal chart is written in internal temperatures, which only a thermometer can read.

item.title: Instant-read or leave-in wireless: which meat thermometer fits the way you cook?
item.description: Retained guide; original date and verification scope apply. One is a pocket tool you stab in and read. The other stays in the meat and pings your phone. They solve different problems, and the listings say which.

item.title: Instant-read or leave-in: which meat thermometer do you actually need?
item.description: Retained guide; original date and verification scope apply. One you push in at the end and read in a second; one you push in at the start and watch from your phone. They answer different questions, and the two thermometers on this site sit at opposite ends of that split.

item.title: Do you need a meat thermometer for an air fryer?
item.description: Retained guide; original date and verification scope apply. USDA's answer is yes, and it is not hedged: always check that food has reached a safe minimum internal temperature with a food thermometer. Here is what its air-fryer page actually says, the numbers to look for, and which of the two thermometers on this site suits a basket.

item.title: Where does the thermometer go in a turkey? Three spots, one number
item.description: Retained guide; original date and verification scope apply. USDA's answer is three places, not one, and the number is the same in all three. Here is the whole procedure on one screen, plus what each kind of thermometer on this site can and cannot do with it.

item.title: Is your meat thermometer accurate? USDA's ice-water check
item.description: Retained guide; original date and verification scope apply. USDA says most food thermometers read within 2 to 4 °F — and that any reading is only right if the probe is in the right place. Checking the first part needs a glass, ice and thirty seconds. Here is how, and what the two thermometers on this site claim about themselves.

item.title: Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?
item.description: Retained guide; original date and verification scope apply. A basket air fryer and a French-door air fryer oven do the same job in very different shapes. Here are the four comparisons that actually decide it - and the one people forget.

item.title: A no-hype checklist for comparing air fryer capacity
item.description: Retained guide; original date and verification scope apply. Quarts on a box are a starting point, not an answer. Six checks that turn a capacity number into 'will my dinner fit?'.

item.title: How to assess cleanup and counter-space trade-offs
item.description: Retained guide; original date and verification scope apply. The appliance you use is the one that is easy to clean and easy to leave out. A practical way to judge both before you buy.

item.title: Questions to ask before buying a multi-function kitchen appliance
item.description: Retained guide; original date and verification scope apply. '10-in-1' sounds like ten appliances for the price of one. Seven honest questions that tell you whether you would use more than two of them.

item.title: Instant-read or leave-in wireless: which meat thermometer fits how you cook?
item.description: Retained guide; original date and verification scope apply. One you dip and pull out in seconds; one you leave in for hours and watch from your phone. They solve different problems - here is how to tell which one is yours.

item.title: Do you need a meat thermometer with an air fryer? The safe temperatures that matter
item.description: Retained guide; original date and verification scope apply. Air fryers brown the outside fast, which is exactly why colour is a poor guide to the inside. The official safe minimum temperatures, and how to check them.
